newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL tin recovers on buying, aided by weak ringgit.
newsitem.headline: KL tin recovers on buying, aided by weak ringgit.

text.p: Malaysian tin recovered the six cents it lost on Monday to return to its previous closing level of 14.65 ringgit ($) a kg on Tuesday following strong buying demand, traders said.
"It went up despite the LME (London Metal Exchange) falling (overnight)," said a trader.
"The demand is good at this level and if the LME just pushes up, we could see the price going up to 15 ringgit (a kg)," added the trader.
Dealers said sentiment was also helped by the weak ringgit against the dollar, which was advantageous to tin exports.
At Tuesday's opening, there were buyers for 159 tonnes and sellers for 99. Final turnover was 132 tonnes, against 102 on Monday, and was absorbed by Japanese, European and local interests.
The closing price was at a premium of $15 against the LME, compared to $30 previously, traders said.
